body:
> The removing steps run the hide popover algorithm, but it started by checking popover validity, which throws if the element is not connected.

So I was going to say that this is the real crux of this issue - both Chromium and Webkit have "before remove steps" which is where these checks happen today. So we don't run into this issue. But then I re-read all of the discussion on https://github.com/whatwg/dom/pull/1185 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9457 and I'm reminded of what a mess this is. E.g. that at least Chromium's "before remove" steps are actually "mid remove" steps.

Given that, I think this solution will "work". It does so by just allowing you to call `hidePopover()` on a popover that is not showing, or isn't in an active document. But I guess you're calling "hide" anyway, so who's to say it didn't work in this case.

TL;DR this looks good. Thanks for putting it up.

@josepharhar for an additional look
